resources.string: Nino has started translating subtitles. Have a great game!
PS5 Games, With Subtitles in Your Language
In games without your language, your phone reads the English subtitles and translates them. You keep playing as usual.
Popular games come with every line pre-translated, at no cost. In those games subtitles show up instantly, even offline; all other games are covered by free translation.
Watch the translation over the game on your TV, or in big letters on your phone. Getting set up only takes a few minutes.
Connect the PS5, TV and phone to one network
Sign in to the PS5 with the second account, go to Settings › System › Remote Play › Pair Device, then type the code it shows into this field.
Switch the PS5 on or put it in rest mode; it appears in this list as soon as it\'s found. The phone and the PS5 need to share a Wi-Fi network.
That doesn\'t look like an IP address. Type it as 192.168.1.20, with no http:// and no port.
You have 5 minutes to use the code. If anything fails, you\'ll see why here.
Linking with the PS5; this takes 30 s at most…
This PSN account is unknown to the PS5. Check that the code came from the PS5 screen you opened while signed in to the second account.
That code was rejected. Get a fresh code on the PS5 and type it in.
Another Remote Play session is using this PS5 right now.
This PS5\'s system software can\'t be used with this version. Update the PS5, then retry.
Remote Play on the PS5 stopped. Restart the PS5 and try again.
Nothing was found at this address. Double-check the PS5\'s IP address.
No response from the PS5. Is the phone on the same Wi-Fi network as the PS5?
The code reached the PS5, but no response came back. Give it another try.
The PS5 connection component could not start on this phone.
Sign in with the PSN account and pair the PS5 first.
The home screen lets you switch this at any time.
The phone sits beside the TV or monitor
While the Nino TV app is open, the phone and the TV find each other on the same Wi-Fi by themselves. The TV app (Samsung, LG, Android TV) can be set up straight from this phone, with no computer.
The translation is shown in big letters on this phone; simply set it down beside the TV or monitor.
How should Nino get the game picture?
Remote Play over Wi-Fi; requires a second PSN account
HDMI capture card on the USB-C port
Connect the card to the USB-C port
Nino gets the PS5 picture through Remote Play on your Wi-Fi. This requires a second PSN account and pairing with the PS5.
Nino gets the Xbox picture through home streaming on your Wi-Fi. You sign in to Microsoft and pick your Xbox; Remote features need to be enabled on the Xbox.

Plug the console (PS5 or Xbox) into the Capture Card\'s HDMI input, then connect the card to this phone by USB-C. There\'s no sign-in or pairing; the translation still shows on the TV or on this phone.
No Capture Card detected. Connect it to the USB-C port; some phones can\'t use external cameras (Android 14 or later is required).
If the card shows only black, go to Settings › System › HDMI › Enable HDCP on the PS5 and switch it off. Xbox games rarely use HDCP.
No camera permission. A Capture Card looks like a camera on Android; give Nino camera permission.
Pull the plug to stop the translation
Tap the Plug to Set Up
TAP THE PLUG OR DRAG IT TO THE SOCKET
Hold the phone horizontally to go full screen
Open the game on your console (PS5 or Xbox), then slide this bar all the way. The phone takes the picture, reads the subtitles and translates them.
Shown over your game on the TV, or here on the phone. Tap to change.
Supported games use ready-made translations, so subtitles show up instantly. This costs nothing.
This is where you manage devices, your PSN account, notifications and the translation engine.
Nino picks the right pack as soon as a game starts. Anything the pack lacks goes to your chosen engine. Packs cost nothing, and new ones and fixes arrive automatically.
If you turn this off, the selected engine translates every line.
There are no packs yet. Go online and tap Update packs.
New packs and fixes download by themselves once a week
The screen won\'t sleep · brightness lowers by itself
Drag inside the frame to move it, or drag a corner to change its size.
Once translation begins, you\'ll see the game picture in this area.

Besides the subtitle, Nino can keep watching up to three small areas, like quest text, a phone message or a notification. Each one is checked roughly every second and translated again only when its text changes. On the TV and on the phone\'s subtitle screen, the translation is placed right where the original text was.

There\'s a newer Nino. Tap the button below, then open the file once it downloads and install it. The old version can stay; the update replaces it and keeps your settings. If installing fails, uninstall the old version first and then install once more.
Versions differ: the %1$s TV has %2$s, this phone has %3$s. Updating takes roughly a minute; leave the TV switched on and on the same Wi-Fi.
This feature isn\'t ready yet. It\'s coming in a future update.
Test line: can you read this on top of the game?
No TV found on the network (the TV may be off; that\'s fine).
No computer, just Wi-Fi · Samsung, LG, Android TV
Share lines with the common pool
Anonymously shares the English lines Nino reads
If none of the packs fit the game, Nino asks you which game it is once, two minutes into translation.
The speaker\'s name is placed in front of the translation (ARTHUR: …) and is left as it is, untranslated.
Read an unchanged subtitle area more often
Even if the subtitle area seems the same, it\'s re-read every 2 frames rather than every 20. This puts more load on the CPU.
Nino sends anonymous error and speed statistics
Nino doesn\'t use accounts; your settings live only on this phone. Both the app and the game packs cost nothing.
Connect the plug and Nino starts on the TV with subtitles flowing.
Slide to begin; translated lines show up above.
Game packs apply only when the target language is Turkish.
Network and PS5 link, picture, translation time

GTA 6 gets its Turkish subtitles from Nino\'s shared translation pool: a strong AI translates every line a single time, so everybody sees the same text. There are no settings or keys to deal with, and it costs nothing.
The key didn\'t work. Check it and try again.
In games that have a ready pack, this engine handles only the lines the pack doesn\'t cover.
Size TV text like the game\'s own subtitles
When on, the TV sizes the text to the English line in the game; changing the size below turns this off.
Drag the slider to the end and the background becomes fully opaque, covering the game\'s English text. The full-width band covers the sides too.
A sample subtitle appears on the TV when you release the slider. In the fixed position you can also move it with the ▲ and ▼ keys on the TV remote.
Cover: the translation covers the game\'s English subtitle. With Above or Below the English subtitle stays visible and the translation sits right above or below it.
Show previous lines above during fast speech
When off, a new line wipes out the one before it. Requires TV app 0.9.16 or newer.

When the PS5 picture is black inside the Nino TV app, pick Overlay: the TV then plays the PS5 through its own HDMI input and lays the subtitle on top. If there\'s no picture at all, the TV app opens the HDMI inputs first and moves to Overlay where supported. The Google Play version of the TV app lacks Overlay, so this setting has no effect there and the TV tells you on screen.
Display the small Nino mark on TV
When off, only the little Nino logo in the lower-left corner of the TV disappears.
Fill this in only if the second account uses a sign-in passcode on the PS5. Nino types it when the PS5 asks for it; it\'s kept encrypted on the phone.
Play Xbox audio on this device
During Xbox remote play, sound comes out of this device; with this off, the game may have no sound.
Ask Nino when you get stuck during setup
Tell us when something isn\'t working
Log out of your Microsoft account
Set up the TV app using this phone
Start translation first for a test subtitle; the text appears once the TV app connects to the phone.
Nino links to your PS5 using Remote Play. Sign in with a second PSN account, which is free and different from the account you play on.
Your own account stays the one you play with on the TV
You sign in on Sony\'s own page
When you switch on the controller to play, pick your MAIN account on the PS5. If you play on the second account that Nino uses, your controller will not work in the game.
The server didn\'t respond in time. Try again.
The internet seems unreachable. Check your connection, then retry.
The PlayStation server gave an unexpected response. Try again.
The account couldn\'t be saved to this phone\'s secure storage.
Too many attempts; wait a few minutes and try again.

If Remote Play uses your own account, it takes over the session you\'re playing and your controller. A second account just watches the picture, while you go on playing with your own account and controller. It costs nothing, and PS Plus isn\'t required.
If the page won\'t open, use the browser sign-in option below.
Sony\'s sign-in page couldn\'t be opened
Neither the internet nor Sony could be reached. Check your connection.
The page did not load in time.
A secure connection couldn\'t be made (are the date and time correct?).
The page came up empty; Sony\'s sign-in screen failed to load in this phone\'s in-app browser.
Android System WebView (the in-app browser) stopped working. Updating it from the Play Store may help.
The page hit an error while loading.
Retry, or sign in with your phone\'s own browser and paste the resulting address here.

When the browser opens, sign in with your second account. Once you\'re done, the browser won\'t send you back to the app; you\'ll be left on a remoteplay.dl.playstation.net page that just says \"redirect\". Tap the address bar, copy the full address, then switch back to Nino. Nino grabs the copied address on its own; if it misses it, paste it into the field below and tap Continue.
Sign in with Google doesn\'t open inside the app (Google doesn\'t allow it), so sign-in moved to the browser. You can still choose \"Sign in with Google\" there.
This address carries no sign-in code. The correct one begins with https://remoteplay.dl.playstation.net/remoteplay/redirect?code=
Nino captures the picture from your console through Wi-Fi.
Uses Remote Play; requires a second PSN account
Xbox Series X|S with just a Microsoft account
Nino gets the PS5 picture through Remote Play. In the next step you\'ll sign in to a second PSN account and pair the PS5.
Nino gets the Xbox picture through home streaming (Remote Play). In the next step you\'ll sign in to Microsoft and pick your Xbox. To use a capture card instead, go to Settings › Picture Input.
Xbox support is still a Beta. If you run into trouble, let us know and we\'ll get on it quickly.
Use the Microsoft account that\'s on your Xbox to sign in. The phone only watches the Xbox\'s home stream, so your game keeps going.
The button gives you a code. Since Microsoft\'s sign-in page can\'t open inside the app, you\'ll type that code at microsoft.com/link in your browser.
The browser couldn\'t be opened. You can open %1$s on another device and enter the code.
Tap the code to copy it:

1. Your code is on the clipboard and microsoft.com/link is open in the browser. If the page didn\'t come up, tap the link above.\n2. Paste the code, sign in with the Microsoft account that\'s on your Xbox, and approve access.\n3. Switch back to Nino; the rest happens automatically.
The Microsoft sign-in has expired. Sign in again from Settings › Console.
The code has expired. Try again.
No Xbox profile is linked to this Microsoft account. Use the account that is signed in on your Xbox.
The internet seems unreachable. Check your connection, then retry.
The Xbox service gave an unexpected response (%1$s).
Xboxes linked to your account. Enable remote features on the Xbox under Settings › Devices & connections › Remote features.
This account has no Xbox linked to it. Sign in to the Xbox with this same account and enable remote features.
Remote play isn\'t enabled: enable Remote features on the Xbox
The phone isn\'t connected to any network
Join this phone to the Wi-Fi of the router your PS5 uses. Nino picks up again on its own.
The phone\'s network dropped and took the PS5 link with it
The phone lost Wi-Fi for a moment and the PS5 link couldn\'t recover. Keep the phone close to the router on a 5 GHz network; a cable between the PS5 and the router helps too.
The PS5 was switched off or entered rest mode
Switch the PS5 on. So Nino can reach it in rest mode too, enable \"Stay connected to the internet\" in the power saving settings.
End the Remote Play session on the other phone, tablet or PC; Nino then picks the link back up by itself.
The PS5 connection dropped and didn\'t come back

There\'s no response from the PS5 on the network. Check that the PS5 and the phone use the same router. If this keeps happening, turn the router off and on, or run a cable to the PS5. Meanwhile Nino keeps retrying.
No connection to the PS5 could be made
Make sure the PS5 is switched on and shares a network with this phone, then begin again.
The phone\'s network cut out during play
The phone\'s network cut out %1$d times. Bring the phone nearer the router and switch to 5 GHz Wi-Fi.
The PS5 picture keeps breaking up on Wi-Fi

The picture is coming through slowly on the phone\'s Wi-Fi, so it stutters and some subtitles get skipped. Bring the phone nearer the router, switch to 5 GHz Wi-Fi and run a cable from the PS5 to the router.
Data from the PS5 picture is getting lost on the network
Connect the PS5 to the router with a cable too; if it\'s already wired, restart the router.
The link cut out %1$d times. Run a cable from the PS5 to the router and keep the phone close to the router.
Translation is lagging: either the internet or the translation service is slow
Translating a line takes %1$s s. Check your internet connection; if that\'s fine, choose the Free engine in Settings.
The TV app is no longer connected to the phone
The TV link cut out %1$d times. Leave Nino open on the TV and make sure the TV and this phone share a network.
The phone\'s network, the PS5 connection, picture smoothness and translation speed. If there\'s a problem, it says what to do.
The phone has no internet and no home network connection.
Mobile data can\'t see the PS5; switch to the Wi-Fi network the PS5 uses.
The Wi-Fi signal is weak. Get closer to the router, switch to 5 GHz and run a cable to the PS5.
No connection for %1$d min; Nino is still retrying
Is the PS5 switched on and on the same network? If you use rest mode, enable both \"Stay connected to the internet\" and \"Enable turning on PS5 from network\" under Settings › Power Saving.
The connection keeps dropping; the network may be weak.
No picture: the PS5 isn\'t connected
The PS5 picture keeps stuttering, so subtitles may come late or get skipped. Wi-Fi is the usual reason.
All %1$d lines came from ready translations (no wait)
No subtitle has appeared on screen yet
Translation is lagging. Your internet may be slow; pick a different translation engine in Settings.
Open Nino on your TV, and check that both TV and phone share one network.
PS5 didn\'t come back for minutes

If something goes wrong, share this with whoever is helping you.

What happened? In which game, and what did you expect?

When the PS5, network or TV drops, Nino sends us a short summary itself: what happened, when, the network type, your device and TV model. No log, subtitles, names or addresses are sent.
To help us fix the issue, your description, photos and (if selected) the app log go to Nino\'s server. Please leave passwords out.
Thank you! Your report reached us.

From this phone, Nino puts the TV app on your Samsung, LG or Android TV and keeps it updated, no computer required. Scanning the network for TVs; you can switch the brand afterwards.

The TV shows Nino\'s waiting screen. Even if it mentions a computer, nothing is wrong; the TV simply waits for the phone. Now start translation on the home screen, and the phone and the TV will find each other automatically.

From this phone, Nino puts the TV app on your Samsung TV, no computer required. The phone and the TV need to share a Wi-Fi network.
Works with Samsung TVs and smart monitors from 2016 onward; support for 2016–2018 models is still experimental.
No Samsung TV showed up. Is the TV on and connected to the same Wi-Fi? You can enter the TV address below yourself (on the TV: Settings › General › Network › Network Status).
Host PC IP points to a different device: %1$s
Enable developer mode on your Samsung TV
1. Open the Apps screen on the TV.
2. Key in 1 2 3 4 5 on the remote (or enter 12345 using the on-screen keyboard) and the developer mode window appears. On certain newer models you need to do this on the Apps › App Settings screen.
3. Switch Developer mode to On, put this phone\'s address in the Host PC IP field and select OK:
The phone\'s address couldn\'t be found; is it on Wi-Fi?
4. Restart the TV: keep the power button on the remote pressed for roughly 2 seconds until the screen goes dark, then switch it on again. A quick tap just sends it to standby.

The first install asks you a single time to sign in to a free Samsung account, because Samsung only accepts the app with a certificate tied to your TV. If the phone gets a new address, you\'ll need to redo the Host PC IP step.

The TV refused this phone. In the developer mode window on the TV, confirm that Host PC IP matches this phone\'s address (%1$s), then turn the TV off and on by holding the power button for around 2 seconds.
The Nino TV app can\'t run on this Samsung TV; only models from 2016 onward are supported.
The Samsung sign-in didn\'t finish. Retry and complete the sign-in on the page that comes up.
Samsung didn\'t provide a signing certificate. Wait a few minutes, then retry.
The TV has a Nino app signed on another device and it couldn\'t be removed. Open Apps on the TV, select Nino, delete it and try again.

The TV didn\'t accept the signing certificate. Make sure the TV is online (it checks the certificate with Samsung) and its date and time are correct (Settings › General › System Manager › Time), then try again. Nino will get a new certificate, so you\'ll sign in with your Samsung account once more.

The TV\'s clock is running behind, so from the TV\'s point of view the new certificate hasn\'t started yet. Correct the date and time on the TV (Settings › General › System Manager › Time), or retry in a few minutes.

The TV blocked the Nino app from installing. This usually happens when the TV\'s Smart Hub remembers an old install. On the TV choose Settings › Support › Device Care › Self Diagnosis › Reset Smart Hub (the PIN is usually 0000), restart the TV, turn developer mode back on and try again. The reset also signs you out of other apps on the TV.
If the TV shows \"Server under maintenance\", it can\'t talk to Samsung\'s servers. Check the TV\'s internet, date and time, turn the TV off and on, and retry.
From this phone, Nino puts the TV app on your LG TV (webOS), no computer required. The phone and the TV need to share a Wi-Fi network.
Requirements: LG\'s Developer Mode app installed on the TV, plus a free LG developer account. Nino renews the developer mode period for you.
No LG TV showed up. Is the TV on and connected to the same Wi-Fi? You can enter the TV address below yourself (on the TV: Settings › General › Network › connected network).
Passphrase (key is stored; enter it only if asked)
Enable developer mode on the LG TV
1. Go to webostv.developer.lge.com and create a free LG developer account.
2. Get the Developer Mode app on the TV from the LG Content Store, sign in to it with your account and enable Dev Mode Status. The TV will then restart.
3. Go back into the Developer Mode app and enable Key Server. Keep the app open; the 6-character Passphrase is shown in the bottom-left corner.
4. Enter the Passphrase in the field above, then tap Install and open. It\'s only asked for on the first install.

Developer mode lasts up to 1000 hours, and Nino renews it automatically whenever the TV shares your Wi-Fi. After a long time without connecting, open the Developer Mode app on the TV and press EXTEND; once it expires, the TV app is removed.
No response from the TV. Check that it\'s on and on the phone\'s Wi-Fi, and that Dev Mode Status is enabled in the Developer Mode app.
Key Server is off. Turn on Key Server in the Developer Mode app on the TV and keep the app open on screen.
The Passphrase isn\'t correct. Compare it with the one on the TV screen.
The TV didn\'t accept the key. Turn on Key Server and type the Passphrase again.
From this phone, Nino puts the Android TV app on your Android TV or Google TV, no computer required. The phone and the TV need to share a Wi-Fi network.
Enable debugging in the TV\'s developer options, and keep it enabled so updates can be installed.
No Android TV showed up. Is the TV on and connected to the same Wi-Fi? You can enter the TV address below (on the TV: Settings › Network & Internet › connected network).
Debugging over the network is enabled (5555)
TV address and port, for example 192.168.1.20:41235
With wireless debugging, add the TV\'s port as well. You\'ll find it as \"IP address & Port\" at the top of the TV\'s Wireless debugging screen (for example 192.168.1.20:41235).
Address and port shown in the pairing window
6-digit pairing code (leave blank if paired before)
When you enter the pairing code, add the address and port from the pairing window too (for example 192.168.1.20:37099).
1. Unlock developer options. On the TV, select the Android TV OS build row 7 times in a row, under Settings › System (or Device Preferences) › About.
2. Under Settings › System › Developer options, enable USB debugging. Some TVs have an extra \"Network debugging\" or \"ADB over network\" option; enable it as well if it\'s there.

3. Tap Install and open. When the TV shows \"Allow USB debugging?\", tick \"Always allow from this computer\" and choose Allow. If it can\'t connect, try the Wireless debugging method (Android 11 and later, Google TV).
2. Enable Developer options › Wireless debugging and go into it. Enter the \"IP address & Port\" value from the top of that screen as the TV address.
3. For the first install, select \"Pair device with pairing code\". Enter the address and port from the pop-up along with the 6-digit code, and tap Install and open before the pop-up closes.

No response from the TV. Check that it\'s on and on the phone\'s Wi-Fi, and that debugging is enabled in developer options. With wireless debugging the port is new each time, so enter the one shown right now.
The TV didn\'t grant debugging access. Retry and select Allow on the TV screen.

Pairing didn\'t work: either the code was wrong or the TV\'s pairing window closed. Reopen the window, enter the fresh code and port, then retry.

Translating subtitles from the Xbox game
Open the game on your console (PS5 or Xbox), then tap the plug or drag it into the socket. The phone takes the picture, reads the subtitles and translates them.

Pick 720p if the connection keeps dropping. Applies from the next connection.
The Xbox could not start the stream.
the Xbox could not start the stream

The Xbox could not open a streaming session. Please check:
1. On the Xbox, Settings › Devices & connections › Remote features is switched on.
2. The power mode is "Sleep" (Instant-on); in energy-saving mode the Xbox cannot be woken remotely.
3. The Xbox and this phone are on the same network.
4. No other stream is running on the Xbox or on another device.
5. Restart the Xbox: hold the power button for 10 seconds, then start translating again once it is back on.
6. Switch Stream quality to 720p in Settings and try again.

The Xbox could not open a streaming session. Please check:
1. On the Xbox, Settings › Devices & connections › Remote features is switched on.
2. The power mode is "Sleep" (Instant-on); in energy-saving mode the Xbox cannot be woken remotely.
